summary: The scouts in Canaan describe themselves as grasshoppers beside the people they saw. Isaiah uses the same comparison for the inhabitants of the earth. Leviticus names the insect as food, and Chronicles pictures it consuming the land.

senses.definition: A small jumping insect, one of the edible kinds in Leviticus and a threat to crops in large numbers.

evidence.note: The list of permitted jumping insects ends with the ḥāgāb and its kind.
The scouts compare their apparent size to that of grasshoppers.
Seen from above the circle of the earth, its inhabitants resemble grasshoppers.
Yahweh speaks of commanding the locust to consume the land.
The grasshopper appears beside the flowering almond and failing caper in a description of old age.

cognates.gloss: possibly locust, in an epithet of Rašap

evidence.locator: SEM000109, UGC001825; compare the epithet in KTU 1.90:2

note: Leviticus distinguishes several named kinds but supplies no species-level description of the ḥāgāb. The Ugaritic form also admits an interpretation as a title relating to guarding, so the insect sense there is uncertain. Ezra 2:46 names a person. The register’s plural ‘sons of Hagab’ identifies his family.
